If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (days 1–5) to compensate for bearish bias.  
When sentiment swings from positive to negative within 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–3% in late horizon (days 20–30) to reflect reversal risk.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast in mid-horizon to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast in early horizon to avoid false optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, apply a 3–5% downward bias across entire forecast horizon to reflect sustained bearish sentiment.
